### chispilla.c1: Broad, adhesive toe pads

Trait ← Need grip on wet rock surfaces ← 1.6-bar air retains high humidity (D8) ← Algal mats form slick biofilm (F15) ← Perpetual moisture dictates locomotion ← F15

- **Skill:** Adhere (Basic): Climb wet surfaces without falling (+25% stability).
- **Weakness:** Pads lose suction on dry, dusty rock.
- **Observe:**
  1. Pads flatten when stepping on wet stone
  2. Climbs vertical tuff walls effortlessly
  3. Shakes water off feet after rain
- **Journal:** They stick to the wet stone like glass beads.
- **Plausibility:** plausible (judge astrobio/foodweb-2026-11-21, 2026-11-21)
  - Permanent humidity at the spring (D8, F15) and slick algal biofilm on tuff favor wet-adhesion or mucus-assisted grip, not Gecko-style dry van der Waals alone. Loss of grip on dry dusty rock matches how many amphibians and some lizards trade wet-surface performance for dry friction.
